FormCapy citation-component distribution

citeproc-js is distributed here under Common Public Attribution License 1.0
(CPAL-1.0), exercising the upstream dual-license choice. The original upstream
dual-license notice is preserved in citeproc.js and citeproc-LICENSE.txt, and
both CPAL-1.0.txt and AGPL-3.0.txt are included. No upstream code was modified,
minified or combined into an application bundle. Application adapter code is
separate and remains under the repository MIT license; MIT does not replace
the licenses of these third-party files.

CPAL attribution (also displayed in the citation assistant):
(c) Frank Bennett
citeproc-js implements the Citation Style Language
https://citationstyles.org/

Source code: citeproc-source.tar.gz contains the upstream core source snapshot at commit
cc9153c45293af878de08cafddbefe6ea150c380, including src/, tools/, the original
processor files and original license notices. citeproc.js is also the directly
readable, unmodified file served to the browser. No network service executes it:
the user's browser performs citation rendering. Local publication, not merely
an upstream link, supplies the corresponding source with the application.
Exact original bytes, archive digest and provenance are in sources.json.
This GitHub source snapshot does not embed optional Git submodule contents;
the selected runtime styles and locale are separately published below. The
original README describes upstream's full external test/build environment.

Citation Style Language styles and locale data:

This product uses the Citation Style Language (CSL) project:
https://citationstyles.org/
The unmodified MLA and APA style files and en-US locale are distributed under
Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 3.0 Unported. CC-BY-SA-3.0.txt contains
the complete license. Authors/contributors/translators and rights metadata
remain exactly as supplied inside each XML file. Original project licensing
statements are in styles-README.md and locales-README.md. Sources and commit
pins are in sources.json. No official manual prose or example papers are
included. These components do not represent institutional endorsement.
